title: Split a sum across devices
starter:
let split_sum (xs : float array) (n : int) : float =
  0.0
hints: Shard d is the s elements starting at d * s, with s = Array.length xs / n. Write a helper part d that returns one partial sum.
In part d, start let p = ref 0.0 and add xs.(d * s + e) for e = 0 to s - 1 with p := !p +. ....
Then start let tot = ref (part 0), add part d for d = 1 to n - 1, in that order, and return !tot.

answer.code:
let split_sum (xs : float array) (n : int) : float =
  let s = Array.length xs / n in
  let part d =
    let p = ref 0.0 in
    for e = 0 to s - 1 do
      p := !p +. xs.(d * s + e)
    done;
    !p
  in
  let tot = ref (part 0) in
  for d = 1 to n - 1 do
    tot := !tot +. part d
  done;
  !tot
answer.explain: Device d adds up its own shard, starting from 0.0 and going left to right, as each device's kernel does. Device 0 then adds the partial sums in device order, starting from partial 0. In floating point the order of the additions decides the bits: with 1e16 and three 1.0s, a plain left-to-right sum loses every 1.0, while the split sum keeps two of them, because the shard of 1.0s is added up first.
